I held off on building anything, because this has the signature of a scam — and a specific, currently-active one that targets developers. Here's my honest read.

## Why this looks like a scam, not a job

**The economics don't make sense.** A "SF-based and backed" startup does not pay a developer **$300/month** (or $600 full-time). That's below US minimum wage by an order of magnitude. Real funded startups in SF pay real salaries. Implausible pay is a classic lure.

**"The application is the interview — build it, show your work."** This is the tell. It's structured to get you to either (a) do substantial unpaid labor, or (b) **clone and run their code/project on your machine**, which is the actual payload in the most common version of this scam.

**The domain is fake.** `8x-internal.com` is not a real company domain. The legitimate company called "8x" is **8x8.com** (a public VoIP company) — completely unrelated. Putting "internal" in a public recruiting link, on a throwaway domain with no web presence, is a phishing pattern.

**The outreach pattern is textbook.** Cold LinkedIn DM, flattery ("cracked dev"), emojis, urgency, a brand-new-looking opportunity, link to an off-platform site. 

**It matches an active malware campaign.** Right now (2025–2026) there's a North-Korea-linked operation called **"Contagious Interview"** that does *exactly this*: fake recruiters on LinkedIn → a "build this app / run this coding task" assignment → you clone a repo or `npm`/`npx` a package → it silently installs a backdoor (OtterCookie / FlexibleFerret). A recent twist: opening their project in **VS Code** and clicking "trust the author" auto-runs their malicious task config. ([Microsoft Security](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/03/11/contagious-interview-malware-delivered-through-fake-developer-job-interviews/), [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/fake-job-recruiters-hide-malware-in-developer-coding-challenges/), [Dark Reading](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/dprk-fake-job-scams-self-propagate-contagious-interview))

## One thing in your folder I want to flag

`C:\Quran-ChatApp` is empty except for a `.mcp.json`. It configures an MCP server that runs `npx -y @_davideast/stitch-mcp` and contains a **live API key embedded in the file**:

```
STITCH_API_KEY": "AQ.Ab8RN6...
```

`@_davideast/stitch-mcp` itself appears to be Google's "Stitch" UI-design tool (by a Google dev advocate), so it may be benign — but **did you create this file, or did it come from them?** That matters:
- If it came from the recruiter, don't run it, and treat that key as theirs (don't use it).
- If it's yours, you still shouldn't keep a plaintext API key in a project file — rotate/revoke it.

## What I'd do

1. **Don't run, clone, `npm install`, `npx`, or open-in-VS-Code anything from `8x-internal.com` or from this "interview."** That's the whole attack.
2. **Don't send money, ID, SSN, or bank details** for "onboarding/equipment/background check."
3. **Verify independently:** find the company's *real* site and careers page; check the recruiter's LinkedIn for account age, real mutual connections, and post history; reverse-image-search the profile photo.
4. **Report** the profile/message to LinkedIn, and optionally to the [FTC](https://reportfraud.ftc.gov).
5. **If you've already run anything they gave you:** disconnect from the network, run a full AV/EDR scan, rotate any credentials/keys (including that Stitch key), and check for unexpected npm packages or processes.

A couple of questions so I can help with the right thing:
- **Did you set up that `.mcp.json` / Stitch yourself, or did it arrive as part of "the assignment"?**
- **Have you run any command, package, or repo from them yet?**

To be clear: building a Qur'an chat app is a perfectly good project, and I'm happy to help you build one **from scratch, your own code, on your terms** — for your portfolio or even to genuinely apply somewhere legit. What I won't do is help execute their code or hand over anything sensitive to that domain. Want to go that route instead?

Sources: [Microsoft Security – Contagious Interview](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/03/11/contagious-interview-malware-delivered-through-fake-developer-job-interviews/) · [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/fake-job-recruiters-hide-malware-in-developer-coding-challenges/) · [Dark Reading – DPRK fake jobs](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/dprk-fake-job-scams-self-propagate-contagious-interview) · [Trend Micro – fake recruiter scams](https://news.trendmicro.com/2025/09/18/fake-recruiter-job-scams/) · [Indeed – interview scam signs](https://www.indeed.com/career-advice/interviewing/interview-scams)

This is the right instinct — for this take-home, the engineering that matters is mostly invisible: how you stop an AI from *inventing scripture*, and how you make it feel beautiful. Typing the React is the easy 20%. Here's the full design, with my recommendation on every fork and the open decisions flagged at the end.

---

## A. What we're actually building (precise scope)

A mobile app where a user asks a question in natural language ("what does the Qur'an say about patience in hardship?", "explain the meaning of Surah Al-Fatiha", "verses about kindness to parents") and gets a **grounded answer that quotes real verses, in Arabic + translation, with exact `surah:ayah` citations** — streamed token-by-token, with the cited verses rendered as tappable cards.

**In scope for v1 (what the reviewer will see):**
- Auth (guest + email) → personalized, persisted chat history
- Streaming chat with grounded answers + citations
- Verse cards: Arabic (Uthmani script) + English translation + reference + copy/share
- Conversation list, light/dark mode, polished empty state with suggested prompts
- The anti-hallucination layer (below) — your headline differentiator

**Explicitly out of v1 (mention as roadmap in the Loom):** audio recitation, tafsir/exegesis, word-by-word, bookmarks, multi-language UI, push notifications, offline mode, Apple Sign-In. Naming these as *deliberately deferred* signals product judgment rather than ignorance.

---

## B. The crux: grounding & religious accuracy (this is what wins)

The single biggest failure mode — and the thing that would instantly discredit a Qur'an app — is an LLM **fabricating a verse** or attaching a real reference to invented words. My whole architecture is built to make that structurally impossible, not just "prompted against":

1. **The model never supplies the scripture text.** Retrieval pulls candidate verses from our verified Supabase DB. Claude receives them as the *only* allowed source and is told to answer strictly from them.
2. **The model returns verse *references*, not verse *text*.** Claude cites `2:153`; the **app renders the canonical Arabic + translation from our DB by that ID.** So even if the model misremembers a word, the displayed verse is always the verified one.
3. **Citation validator.** Before display, we check every `surah:ayah` Claude cited actually exists in the retrieved set. If it cites something we didn't give it → we flag/strip it. This is a small, very demo-able feature ("watch — it literally cannot cite a verse that isn't real").
4. **Humility guardrails.** System prompt forbids issuing rulings (*fatwa*), keeps a reverent neutral tone, defers interpretation/jurisprudence to qualified scholars, and shows a persistent *"study aid, not a religious authority"* disclaimer. This also sidesteps sectarian landmines.
5. **Graceful "I don't know."** If retrieval finds nothing relevant, the answer is "I couldn't find a verse directly addressing this" — never a confident fabrication.

That layered defense is the strongest thing you can say in a 4-minute video, and most applicants won't have thought about it.

---

## C. Data layer — dataset, translation, licensing

**The Arabic text itself is not copyrighted** (it's divine text), **but specific digital encodings, fonts, and translations are.** So we use verified sources and attribute properly — correct *and* respectful.

**Source options (I'd seed our own DB once, not depend on a live third-party API at runtime):**
- **[Quranic Universal Library (QUL)](https://qul.tarteel.ai/)** by Tarteel — downloadable JSON: Uthmani script, word-by-word, many translations, tafsir, audio. My top pick for completeness.
- **[Al Quran Cloud API](https://alquran.cloud/api)** — dead-simple REST, Uthmani + many translations + audio; great for fast seeding.
- **[fawazahmed0/quran-api](https://github.com/fawazahmed0/quran-api)** — 400+ translations, CDN JSON, very permissive license; easiest bulk seed.
- **Tanzil / KFGQPC** — the canonical verified Uthmani text upstream of most of the above.

**Translation edition is a real decision** (tone + licensing differ):
- **Saheeh International** — clear modern English, widely permitted to distribute. **My recommended default.**
- **The Clear Quran (Dr. Mustafa Khattab)** — very readable, popular, but check its license terms.
- **Yusuf Ali / Pickthall** — public domain, but archaic English.

**Postgres schema (Supabase):**
```
surahs(id, name_ar, name_en, name_translit, revelation_place, ayah_count, order)
verses(id, surah_id, ayah_no, text_uthmani, text_simple,
       translation_en, translation_edition, juz, page, embedding vector(384))
conversations(id, user_id, title, created_at)
messages(id, conversation_id, role, content, cited_verse_ids int[], created_at)
```
6,236 verses + 384-dim embeddings is tiny — fits the **Supabase free tier** with room to spare.

---

## D. Retrieval / RAG design

Mapping a free-form question → the right verses is the interesting ML problem. Options:

| Approach | Quality | Build cost | Extra key? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Postgres full-text search** (tsvector over translation) | OK on keywords, weak on concepts | Lowest | No |
| **Semantic (embeddings + pgvector)** | Strong on topics/synonyms | Medium | Maybe |
| **Hybrid (FTS + vector, reranked)** | Best | Highest | Maybe |

**Embeddings sub-decision:**
- **`gte-small` via Supabase Edge Functions** — free, in-DB, 384-dim, ~MTEB 61. **My v1 recommendation** — no extra API key, embed all 6,236 verses once.
- **OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small`** or **Voyage** — a few % better recall, costs cents to seed, one more key. Easy upgrade later.

**My call:** ship v1 on **gte-small semantic search (top-k ≈ 6–8 verses)**, structured so we can bolt on hybrid reranking later. We embed the **English translation** (questions come in English) and store the Arabic for display.

---

## E. AI layer — Claude

- **Model: `claude-sonnet-4-6`** — the sweet spot of quality/latency/cost for grounded chat. (`claude-haiku-4-5` for a cheap mode; Opus is overkill for this infra budget.)
- **Prompt caching** on the system prompt + instruction block → cheaper, faster repeat calls (I'll wire this via the `claude-api` skill so it's done correctly).
- **Structured output:** Claude returns streamed prose **plus** a machine-readable list of cited verse IDs (tool call / JSON), so the app renders verse cards from the DB and the validator can run. This is the keystone of the anti-hallucination design.
- **System prompt encodes:** role (humble study companion), hard rules (only provided verses, exact citations, no fabrication, no fatwa, defer to scholars), tone, language matching, and graceful-unknown behavior.

---

## F. Backend — Vercel, streaming, security

- **`/api/chat`** (Vercel function): authenticates the request → retrieves verses from Supabase → calls Claude with streaming → streams **SSE** back to the phone. The **Anthropic key is a server-only Vercel env var** — never in the app bundle.
- **Limits are fine for us:** Hobby tier standard functions run 60s (up to 300s with Fluid compute); Edge streaming allows up to 300s if the first byte ships within 25s — our answers are seconds. I'll likely use the **Edge runtime** for lowest-latency streaming (Anthropic SDK supports fetch/edge). ([Vercel limits](https://vercel.com/docs/functions/limitations))
- **Abuse protection (important — the endpoint is public):** require a valid **Supabase JWT** to hit `/api/chat` (only signed-in/guest-session users), plus a simple per-user rate limit. This protects your API spend.

---

## G. Frontend — Expo, Arabic typography, design

This is half the grade, so it gets real attention.

- **Stack:** Expo (SDK 51+) + **Expo Router**, run on your iPhone via **Expo Go**. Hermes engine gives us `fetch` streaming.
- **The RN streaming gotcha** (verified, and where most devs trip): React Native has **no `EventSource`**. The reliable path is **`expo/fetch` streaming** (or `react-native-sse`) with a **buffering SSE parser** — one `read()` can return multiple or partial events, so naive parsing throws intermittent JSON errors in production. I'll wire `AbortController` to a **stop button** and restart-on-fail. ([getwireai guide](https://getwireai.com/blog/react-native-llm-streaming), [Expo fetch docs](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/sdk/expo/))
- **Arabic rendering / RTL:** render Arabic blocks with `writingDirection: 'rtl'` + `textAlign: 'right'` — **without** forcing whole-app RTL (`I18nManager.forceRTL`), which would flip the English chrome and cause pain. English UI stays LTR; only verse text is RTL.
- **Fonts:** **KFGQPC HAFS Uthmanic Script** for ayah display (the authentic standard reviewers recognize; free to use/distribute, not modifiable), with **Amiri / Scheherazade New** (SIL OFL, freely usable) as fallback, and **Inter** for English UI. Loaded via `expo-font`. ([KFGQPC data](https://github.com/thetruetruth/quran-data-kfgqpc), [Scheherazade/SIL](https://software.sil.org/scheherazade/))
- **Design language:** calm, reverent, modern — generous whitespace, a subtle Islamic-geometric accent, beautiful typography, light/dark, smooth token-stream animation, haptics on send, animated verse-card reveal, skeleton loaders, a thoughtful empty state with suggested prompts. **This is exactly where we bring in Stitch** to generate a cohesive design system/screens, then implement them.

---

## H. Auth & persistence

- **Supabase Auth:** offer **"continue as guest" (anonymous)** for zero-friction demo + **email OTP** for real accounts. **Apple Sign-In** looks great on iOS but needs a $99 Apple dev account — defer.
- **RLS policies** so users only ever read their own conversations/messages.
- Persist conversations + messages; show a history drawer.

---

## I. Cost to build + demo

- **Anthropic:** pennies per chat with Sonnet + caching; a full demo is well under a dollar. Needs a funded key (**~$5 minimum**) — the only required spend.
- **Supabase / Vercel / gte-small embeddings:** all **free tier**.
- **Net:** ≈ **$5 + your time.** (OpenAI/Voyage embeddings, if you upgrade, add cents.)

---

## J. How we win on the two stated criteria

They literally said *UI/UX is a hard criterion* and want a 4-min Loom (face + features + design decisions + code). So the **Loom script** I'd target:
1. **0:00–0:20** — who you are, one-line pitch.
2. **0:20–1:20** — the *hard problem*: how you guarantee it never fabricates scripture (render-from-DB + citation validator). **This is your moat.**
3. **1:20–2:50** — live demo on the iPhone: ask 2–3 questions, show streaming, verse cards, history, dark mode.
4. **2:50–3:50** — architecture + code: RAG flow, key-on-server, Edge streaming, RLS.
5. **3:50–4:00** — roadmap (audio, tafsir) + close.

We optimize the build for "always has something demoable," and front-load the two graded axes: **grounding** and **polish**.

---

## K. Milestone sequencing (each step is independently demoable)

1. **Expo app + chat UI shell** running on your iPhone (mock responses) — *no keys needed.*
2. **Seed Supabase** with verses + translation + embeddings.
3. **`/api/chat` → Claude** streaming, key server-side.
4. **Wire RAG** + citation validation + verse cards.
5. **Auth + persistence** (guest/email, history).
6. **UI/UX polish pass** with Stitch + record the Loom.

---

## L. Top risks (and the mitigation)

- **Hallucinated verses** → render-from-DB + validator (§B).
- **Translation licensing** → pick a clearly-permitted edition + attribute (§C).
- **Doctrinal/sectarian sensitivity** → stick to text + translation, defer interpretation, neutral tone, disclaimer.
- **RN streaming flakiness** → `expo/fetch` + buffered SSE parser + abort/retry (§G).
- **Public endpoint abuse** → JWT-gated + rate limit (§F).
- **Scope creep** → ruthless v1 line (§A).

---

## M. Decisions I need from you

Here's where I want your input — my recommendation is in **bold**, but tell me where you differ:

1. **Translation edition?** → **Saheeh International** (clear, freely distributable). Or The Clear Quran / Yusuf Ali?
2. **Retrieval for v1?** → **gte-small semantic search** (free, no extra key). Or simplest FTS, or go straight to hybrid?
3. **Claude model?** → **Sonnet 4.6** default (+ optional Haiku "cheap mode"). OK?
4. **Auth for v1?** → **Guest + email OTP**, defer Apple Sign-In. OK?
5. **Audio recitation in v1 or roadmap?** → I'd **defer to roadmap** to protect the timeline. Agree?
6. **Anthropic API key** — do you already have a funded one, or want me to walk you through getting one when we reach §K-step 3?
7. Anything about the **product vision** you'd add/cut? (e.g., a "verse of the day", tafsir, a specific audience.)

Tell me your calls on these (or just say "your defaults are good"), and we'll go as deep as you want on any single section before writing code.

---

## 1. Going fully free — the $0 stack

Every paid piece has a free replacement. Here's the swap:

| Layer | Was (paid) | **Now (free)** |
|---|---|---|
| LLM | Claude API | **Google AI Studio — Gemini 2.5 Flash**: 1,500 req/day, 1M context, *no credit card*. Backup: **Groq** (Llama 3.3 70B, ~315 tok/s, great for streaming) |
| Embeddings | OpenAI/Voyage | **gte-small in Supabase** (free, in-DB) or **Gemini `text-embedding-004`** (free) |
| Voice in (STT) | — | **`expo-speech-recognition`** — on-device (iOS Speech framework), free, no API |
| Voice out (TTS) | — | **`expo-speech`** — on-device, free |
| Verse recitation | — | **Pre-recorded reciter MP3s** (EveryAyah / QUL) — free *and* the correct way (never TTS the Arabic) |
| Storyboard art | — | **Cloudflare Workers AI (FLUX-schnell, ~100k/day free)** / Pollinations / HF — **pre-generated once**, stored in Supabase |
| Host + DB | Vercel/Supabase | same — **free tiers** |

**Total: $0.** Two honest caveats: free LLM tiers are **rate-limited** (Gemini's 1,500/day is plenty for a demo), and Gemini's *free* tier may **use your data for training** — fine for a public portfolio project, but worth knowing. ([Free LLM API rankings 2026](https://costbench.com/best/best-llm-api-with-free-tier/), [TokenMix tested limits](https://tokenmix.ai/blog/free-llm-api))

One note since it can feel confusing: **I'm Claude (Anthropic) helping you *build*; your *app* will run on Gemini/Groq.** No conflict — the coding assistant and the app's model are separate things.

**My recommendation:** Gemini 2.5 Flash as the brain (huge context lets us stuff tafsir + story context in cheaply), Groq as a fast fallback.

---

## 2. "Where do the documents come from?" — your RAG corpus

In RAG, the *"documents"* are the corpus you chunk → embed → retrieve over. For this app it's **layered**, and all of it is free:

| Layer | What it gives | Free source |
|---|---|---|
| **Qur'an text + translation** | the verses themselves | [QUL (Tarteel)](https://qul.tarteel.ai/), [Al Quran Cloud](https://alquran.cloud/api), [fawazahmed0/quran-api](https://github.com/fawazahmed0/quran-api) |
| **Tafsir** (exegesis) | what verses *mean* | **[spa5k/tafsir_api](https://github.com/spa5k/tafsir_api)** — 25+ tafsirs incl. **Ibn Kathir**, JSON, *no rate limit, self-hostable* |
| **Asbāb al-Nuzūl** (occasions of revelation) | **THE "story behind the verse"** | Al-Wāhidī, English trans. Mokrane Guezzou — served via [spa5k/tafsir_api](https://github.com/spa5k/tafsir_api) and [altafsir PDF](https://www.altafsir.com/Books/Asbab%20Al-Nuzul%20by%20Al-Wahidi.pdf) |
| **Revelation chronology / seerah** | the **timeline** (Meccan/Medinan, event order) | derivable from QUL metadata + Qisas al-Anbiya |
| **Stories of the Prophets** | narrative arcs for storyboards | Qisas al-Anbiya (Ibn Kathir) |

**Asbāb al-Nuzūl is the key find** — it's the classical Islamic genre that records *exactly* "why/when this verse was revealed." That's the literal data backbone of your storyboard feature.

**How we build the index:** download → normalize to JSON → chunk (one record per verse, per tafsir segment, per asbāb entry) → embed → store in Supabase pgvector with metadata `{surah, ayah, source, type}`. At query time we filter by `type`: a factual question retrieves verses+tafsir; "tell me the story behind this" retrieves asbāb + Qisas.

**Accuracy caution (matters for this audience):** tafsir and asbāb narrations vary in authenticity — some are weak (*da'īf*). We always **cite the source**, keep the *"study aid, not a religious authority — verify with a scholar"* disclaimer, and never present a narration as definitive. That care is itself a selling point.

*(Technical docs you'll also want bookmarked: [Gemini API](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs), [Supabase pgvector](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/extensions/pgvector), [Expo](https://docs.expo.dev/).)*

---

## 3. Voice assistant — fully on-device, $0

A real voice loop, no cloud API:
- **Tap mic → `expo-speech-recognition`** (Apple's on-device Speech framework) transcribes → feeds the normal RAG flow. ([jamsch/expo-speech-recognition](https://github.com/jamsch/expo-speech-recognition))
- **Answer read aloud** via **`expo-speech`** (device TTS), as a toggle. ([Expo Speech](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/sdk/speech/))
- **The verse itself plays a real reciter's recording** (EveryAyah MP3), *not* TTS — more authentic and respectful.
- UX touches: animated waveform while listening, "tap to speak," auto-play recitation of the cited verse.

---

## 4. The storyboard + timeline — brilliant idea, with one hard rule

I genuinely love this. Many Qur'anic passages *are* narratives (Yusuf is a complete story; Musa, Nuh, Maryam, the People of the Cave…), and a **timeline + visual storyboard** is a fantastic comprehension tool that no generic "Qur'an chatbot" will have. It's your standout feature.

**But here's the constraint we must design around — and it's not optional for this app/audience:**

> **Depicting prophets visually is prohibited by scholarly consensus in Islam** and considered deeply disrespectful. A manga that *draws the face/body of Yusuf, Musa, or any prophet* wouldn't read as a style choice to a Muslim founder — it could be an **instant disqualifier**, and it would genuinely offend many of your users. ([IslamQA](https://islamqa.info/en/answers/181704/), [Egypt's Dar al-Iftā](https://www.dar-alifta.org/en/fatwa/details/10769/), [Aniconism in Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aniconism_in_Islam))

You almost certainly know this — but because it's central to the feature, we bake it into the architecture, not leave it to chance. And the great part: **the same constraint that big Islamic films work under gives us a more distinctive, more tasteful art style** — and *showing* the reviewer we understand it is a massive trust signal. The techniques the pros use (e.g. *The Message*, the animated *Muhammad: The Last Prophet*):

- **Figure-free / aniconic panels** — depict the *setting and symbols*, never the prophet: the **well and the caravan** (Yusuf), the **parted sea and the staff** (Musa), the **ark on the floodwaters** (Nuh), the **cave and the dog** (Ashāb al-Kahf), the **cradle under the palm** (Maryam).
- **POV / first-person** — the scene *through* the prophet's eyes.
- **Light, silhouette, aura, implied presence** — the standard cinematic solution.
- **Calligraphy + geometric motifs** as panel design.

We enforce this in the image prompts as hard rules + **negative prompts** (`no human faces, no depiction of prophets, symbolic scenery only`).

**The pipeline (free, safe, fast):**
1. **Curate ~6–10 narrative stories** for v1 (not "any verse" — that's the scope trap).
2. For each, Gemini + the asbāb/tafsir/Qisas corpus generates a **panel script** (caption + setting + linked verses).
3. **Pre-generate** the figure-free art *once* (Cloudflare FLUX-schnell / Pollinations), **eyeball each panel for appropriateness**, store in Supabase Storage. App serves instantly → no live-gen cost, latency, or safety surprise on stage.
4. **Timeline view:** render the story's events as a vertical chronology, each node linking to its verses + panel + recitation.
5. **Graceful fallback:** for a verse with no curated story, show the **text "story behind it"** (asbāb al-nuzūl) + timeline, and say so — no silent gaps, no improvised images.

---

  • verse cards + reciter audio   ──HTTPS──▶ /api/chat  ──retrieve──▶  verses + tafsir +
  • storyboard + timeline view               /api/story              asbāb (pgvector)
                                                 │                    conversations/messages

                                          (RAG answer + panel script)
```

Straight answer: **no — for a prophet, hiding just the face isn't considered enough by mainstream (Sunni) scholarship.** And there's a near-perfect real-world test case that settles it.

## The decisive precedent

Majid Majidi's 2015 film *Muhammad: The Messenger of God* did **far more** than hide the face. It showed only the baby's **hands and legs**, the **back of his head** as an adolescent, and his **shadow** — the face was *never* on screen. Despite all that caution, **Al-Azhar** (the most authoritative Sunni institution) called for it to be **banned**, with the ruling: *"Shariah prohibits embodying the prophets."* ([Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/irans-muhammad-film-slammed-for-showing-back-of-prophets-head/), [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad:_The_Messenger_of_God_(film)), [RFE/RL](https://www.rferl.org/a/sunni-scholars-call-for-ban-iranian-prophet-muhammad-film/27215186.html))

So your proposed "hide the face, keep the body" is **less** cautious than a film that hid everything but the silhouette — and that film was still rejected.

## Why the face isn't the point

Your intuition is reasonable — *face = identity, so blur it and you've anonymized the person*. But the ruling doesn't hinge on facial recognition. The objection is to **embodiment / impersonation** — representing the prophet's *person* at all. A visible body clearly acting as the prophet **is** the embodiment, face or no face. The stated reasons: it lowers his dignified status, and an actor/figure that "is" the prophet in one frame and something else elsewhere degrades him. ([IslamQA](https://islamqa.info/en/answers/181704), [IslamWeb](https://www.islamweb.net/en/fatwa/475279/portraying-prophets-and-messengers))

Two more things that matter for your design:
- **It applies to *all* prophets**, not just Muhammad — so Musa, Yusuf, Nuh, etc. are all in scope. ([IslamOnline](https://fiqh.islamonline.net/en/depicting-the-prophets-in-films/))
- **Sunni vs. Shia differ** — Shia tradition is more lenient (which is *why* an Iranian film attempted it). Since your app targets the whole Muslim world and is being judged by a Muslim founder, you design to the **stricter Sunni standard** — that way it's safe for everyone. ([Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/release-prophet-muhammad-biopic-divides-sunni-and-shia-muslims-303314))

## What this means for the storyboard (and it still works great)

The rule only restricts the **prophet figure** — *not* the rest of the scene. So you keep full narrative clarity by carrying it with everything *around* the prophet:

- **Prophet's presence** → a **beam/orb of light**, **POV** (we see the scene as if through his eyes), or simple **absence** with the world reacting to him. (Avoid even a shadow/silhouette *of the prophet specifically* — that's exactly what got Majidi criticized.) This is the established film/animation technique. ([Muhammad: The Last Prophet, 2002 anime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_in_film) reached wide distribution doing exactly this.)
- **Non-prophet characters are fine to draw** — Pharaoh and his court, Yusuf's brothers, the caravan merchants, the crowds. They're ordinary people, not prophets.
- **Environment + symbols carry the story** — the staff, the parted sea, the well, the ark, the cradle and palm.

**Concrete example — "Musa parts the sea":** a panel showing a **staff raised inside a shaft of light**, the **sea splitting**, **Pharaoh's army** massing in the distance, the **Israelites** crossing. No Musa figure at all — yet anyone looking knows instantly *this is Musa's story*. You lose nothing; you gain a distinctive, reverent style that signals to the founder you actually understand the subject.

That last point is the real win: getting this *right* is a stronger portfolio signal than the art itself. A generic chatbot won't have thought about it; you will.

---

## Figure-free rules for *this* story

Only two characters are prophets and therefore **never drawn** — represented by **light / POV / symbol / absence**:
- **Yusuf** and **Ya'qub** (Jacob).

**Everyone else is fair to depict** — the brothers, the caravan, al-Aziz, his wife, the noblewomen, the king, the prisoners, Benjamin. That's plenty of human material to anchor each scene.

**Two recurring motifs carry the whole arc** (great for visual cohesion):
1. **The shirt** — bloodied (12:18) → torn from behind (12:25) → cast over the father's face (12:93). A single object threads the beginning, middle, and end.
2. **The eleven stars + sun + moon** — opens the story (the dream, 12:4) and closes it (fulfilled, 12:100).

---

## The "story behind it" (the asbāb / context card)

> Surah Yusuf is **Meccan**, revealed during a period of intense hardship as **consolation** — the only surah that tells one prophet's story start-to-finish, framed as *aḥsan al-qaṣaṣ*, "the best of stories" (12:3). *(Narrations on the precise occasion of revelation vary in authenticity — in-app we'd cite the source and flag it, per our accuracy rule.)*

This text sits at the top of the storyboard as the framing card before panel 1.

---

Each node is both a **timeline point** and a **swipeable panel**. 13 beats, full arc:

| # | Beat | Verses | Visual (figure-free) | Caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Ya'qub = a lamp-lit doorway, prayer beads. | *Young Yusuf tells his father a dream: eleven stars, the sun, and the moon, bowing before him. His father senses greatness — and warns him to keep it secret.* |
| 2 | **The Envy** | 12:7–10 | Ten brothers (drawn) around a fire, faces hard, gesturing toward a small **glowing empty space** and a distant well. | *His brothers burn with envy. One pleads: do not kill him — cast him into the well.* |
| 3 | **Into the Well** | 12:11–15 | **POV from the well floor** looking up: a bright circle of sky, ropes and the brothers' hands lowering a bucket, a warm glow where the viewer stands. Yusuf never drawn — *you are in his place*. | *They carry Yusuf away and lower him into the dark. Unseen, he is reassured: one day you will remind them of this.* |
| 4 | **The False Blood** | 12:16–18 | Brothers weeping at a tent door at night, holding out a **blood-stained shirt** (close-up); an empty prayer mat (Ya'qub). | *At nightfall: "A wolf devoured him." They show his shirt, stained with false blood. Their father answers: "Beautiful patience."* |
| 5 | **The Caravan** | 12:19–20 | Desert caravan at a well at dawn; a water-drawer hauls a bucket **spilling warm light**; coins change hands. Yusuf = the light. | *A passing caravan draws water. "Good news — a boy!" They sell him for a few coins.* |
| 6 | **Sold into Egypt** | 12:21–22 | Grand Egyptian estate gates; **al-Aziz (drawn)** directing servants; a **doorway of light** crossing the threshold. | *In Egypt, al-Aziz tells his wife to treat him honorably. So We established Yusuf in the land.* |

"My Lord has been gracious to me."* |

## How a panel actually gets generated (free pipeline)

We pre-generate each panel once with a **reusable style block + hard negative prompt**, eyeball it, and store it in Supabase Storage. Example for **Panel 3 (the well POV)**:

**Style preamble (shared by all panels):**
```
reverent graphic-novel / manga style, warm earthy desert palette,
dramatic chiaroscuro lighting, subtle Islamic geometric border,
cinematic composition, no text, no lettering
```

**Negative prompt (shared, non-negotiable):**
```
no prophet figures, no depiction of Yusuf, no depiction of Jacob/Ya'qub,
no Prophet Muhammad, no human face or body at the focal/sacred point,
no halos, no idols, no worship imagery
```

**Panel-3 prompt:**
```
View from the bottom of an ancient stone desert well looking straight up:
a bright circle of pale dawn sky far above, frayed ropes and a wooden bucket
descending, several silhouetted hands at the rim lowering it, a soft warm glow
on the empty well floor where the viewer stands, damp mossy stone walls.
No people inside the well. No figure at the bottom.
```

## The system prompt

```text
You are the STORYBOARD ENGINE for a Qur'an study app. You convert a user's
request into ONE strict JSON "panel script" that the app renders as a visual
timeline + swipeable storyboard. You never address the user in prose — your
entire response is a single JSON object that matches the SCHEMA below.

════════════════════════════════════════
SACRED ACCURACY — NON-NEGOTIABLE
════════════════════════════════════════
1. GROUNDING ONLY. You are given a <GROUNDING> block with verses (each has an
   id, Arabic, and translation) and optionally tafsir and asbāb al-nuzūl
   entries. Build the story ONLY from events supported by this material.
   Never invent verses. Never invent events not present in the grounding.
2. NEVER QUOTE SCRIPTURE YOURSELF. Captions are YOUR plain-language paraphrase
   of events. The app displays the real verse text from its own database using
   the ids you cite. Put no Arabic and no quoted Qur'an in any caption.
3. CITE ONLY PROVIDED VERSES. Every id in `verseIds` MUST appear in <GROUNDING>.
   If a beat cannot be anchored to a provided verse, drop that beat. Cite the
   tightest ayah range that covers the beat.
4. SOURCE THE CONTEXT. `contextCard` (the "story behind") must derive from the
   provided tafsir/asbāb. If the grounding flags a narration as weak (da'īf),
   preserve that caveat. If no context is provided, set `contextCard` to "".

════════════════════════════════════════
DEPICTION RULES — NON-NEGOTIABLE
════════════════════════════════════════
5. PROPHETS ARE NEVER DEPICTED. Identify every prophet who appears and list
   them in `figureFreeCharacters`. In EVERY `imagePrompt`, a prophet may be
   represented ONLY by: a beam/orb of light, point-of-view framing, a symbolic
   object, or absence — never a face, body, or silhouette. Non-prophet
   characters (e.g. kings, crowds, non-prophet family) MAY be depicted.
6. Each `imagePrompt` must (a) describe what IS shown and (b) end with an
   explicit exclusion, e.g. "No figure of Yusuf; no face or body of any prophet."
   Never depict God, idols, acts of worship, or angels as figures.

════════════════════════════════════════
TONE
════════════════════════════════════════
7. Reverent, accurate, neutral. No rulings (fatwā), no sectarian positions, no
   personal interpretation of disputed matters. You are a study aid, not an
   authority.

════════════════════════════════════════
DECISION LOGIC — set `status`
════════════════════════════════════════
"ok"                  → grounding supports a coherent narrative you can board.
"no_story"            → valid request but not a narrative (e.g. a thematic or
                        legal question). One-line note in `message`; the app
                        will answer it as normal chat instead. Omit `story`.
"insufficient_context"→ grounding lacks enough verses/context for a faithful
                        story. Say what's missing in `message`. Omit `story`.
"declined"            → request asks to depict a prophet/sacred figure, or is
                        disrespectful/off-topic. Brief kind explanation in
                        `message`; offer the figure-free alternative if relevant.
                        Omit `story`.

════════════════════════════════════════
PROPHETS (keep figure-free if they appear)
════════════════════════════════════════
Ādam, Idrīs, Nūh, Hūd, Sālih, Ibrāhīm, Lūt, Ismā'īl, Ishāq, Ya'qūb, Yūsuf,
Ayyūb, Shu'ayb, Mūsā, Hārūn, Dhul-Kifl, Dāwūd, Sulaymān, Ilyās, Al-Yasa',
Yūnus, Zakariyyā, Yahyā, 'Īsā, Muhammad (peace be upon them all).
Also keep Maryam and any angels figure-free. If unsure whether a named figure
is a prophet, treat them as figure-free.

════════════════════════════════════════
SCHEMA (return exactly this shape, no markdown, no commentary)
════════════════════════════════════════
{
  "status": "ok | no_story | insufficient_context | declined",
  "message": "string — short note shown to user when status != ok; else ''",
  "story": {
    "id": "kebab-case-id",
    "title": "string",
    "surah": 12,
    "contextCard": "string — grounded story-behind, with source + caveat if weak",
    "figureFreeCharacters": ["Yūsuf", "Ya'qūb"],
    "motifs": ["the shirt", "eleven stars and the moon"],
    "panels": [
      {
        "n": 1,
        "title": "string (≤ 6 words)",
        "verses": "12:4-6",
        "verseIds": ["12:4", "12:5", "12:6"],
        "caption": "string (≤ 240 chars, plain paraphrase, no quoted scripture)",
        "imagePrompt": "string — figure-free scene; ends with the exclusion clause",
        "motif": "string or null",
        "recitation": "12:4"
      }
    ]
  }
}

PANELS: 6–12, chronological. Pick 1–2 recurring `motifs` for visual cohesion.
Bookend the arc in the first and last panels when possible.

════════════════════════════════════════
SELF-CHECK BEFORE OUTPUT
════════════════════════════════════════
(a) every `verseId` exists in <GROUNDING>;
(b) no prophet is described as a visible figure in any `imagePrompt`;
(c) no scripture is quoted in any `caption`;
(d) JSON is valid and matches SCHEMA exactly.
Fix any violation, then output.
```

And the **user-turn** that accompanies it each call looks like:

```text
USER REQUEST: "tell me the story behind the verses about Yusuf and his brothers"

<GROUNDING>
[12:4] {ar:"...", en:"O my father, I saw eleven stars..."}
[12:7] {ar:"...", en:"Certainly were there in Joseph and his brothers signs..."}
... (retrieved verses)
[TAFSIR 12:18 — Ibn Kathir] "..."
[ASBAB 12:x — al-Wāhidī, grade: ...] "..."
</GROUNDING>
```

---

## How it works — the pipeline around the prompt

```
user question
   │
   ▼
RETRIEVAL (Supabase pgvector)  ──►  fills <GROUNDING> with verses + tafsir + asbāb
   │
   ▼
GEMINI 2.5 Flash  ◄── system prompt (cached)  +  responseSchema (JSON mode)
   │   outputs panel-script JSON
   ▼
VALIDATION LAYER (your code, not trust)
   │   • every verseId ∈ grounding? strip/repair if not
   │   • each imagePrompt contains the exclusion clause?
   │   • status handled (ok / no_story / insufficient / declined)
   ▼
IMAGE PIPELINE (only for status=ok)
   │   • generate each panel via Cloudflare FLUX / Pollinations
   │   • SAFETY GATE (see below) → cache to Supabase Storage
   ▼
RENDER → timeline view + storyboard view + verse cards + recitation
```

## Why each part is shaped this way

**1. Grounding-only + "never quote scripture yourself" (rules 1–2).** This is the anti-hallucination core. The model's job is *narration and structure*, not *scripture*. It cites verse **IDs**; the app pulls the canonical Arabic + translation from your database and renders those. So even if the model's paraphrase drifts, the actual Qur'an the user sees is always the verified text. Captions are explicitly *paraphrase*, never presented as quotation — that closes the door on "the AI made up a verse."

**2. Cite-only-provided + tightest range (rule 3).** Because retrieval populates `<GROUNDING>`, "only cite what's in grounding" makes every citation **machine-verifiable**. Your validation layer rejects any `verseId` not in the grounding set — the model literally cannot smuggle in a reference that wasn't retrieved.

**3. The `status` enum (decision logic).** Not every question is a story. "What does the Qur'an say about patience?" is thematic, not narrative — so the model returns `no_story` and your app falls back to normal grounded chat. If retrieval came back thin, `insufficient_context` prevents a hallucinated storyboard. And `declined` handles the landmine: "draw the Prophet Muhammad" → polite refusal + offer the figure-free version. This one field lets the app route every input correctly instead of forcing a storyboard onto things that shouldn't be one.

**4. Figure-free enforced in *two* places (rules 5–6).** The `figureFreeCharacters` list tells the app who's sacred; the per-panel **exclusion clause** ("No figure of Yusuf…") gets passed straight into the image model as part of its prompt. The prophet list is hard-coded in the system prompt so the model doesn't have to *recall* who's a prophet — it just matches names. "If unsure, treat as figure-free" makes the failure mode safe-by-default.

**5. Structured output is enforced by the API, not hope.** Gemini supports `responseMimeType: "application/json"` + a `responseSchema`. You set the schema in the API call; the prompt's job is *content quality and safety*, the schema's job is *shape*. Clean separation: the model can't return malformed JSON, and the prompt can focus on the rules.

**6. Cache the system prompt.** It's long and 100% static — perfect for Gemini's context caching. The big rules/prophet/schema block is cached once; each request only pays for the user question + grounding. Cheaper and faster, which matters on a free tier with daily limits.

## The one part that *can't* be fully automated (and the honest fix)

Generating the **panel-script JSON** automatically is safe — it's text, fully validatable. Generating the **images** automatically is the risk: image models *ignore negative prompts sometimes* and may draw a human figure where a prophet should be light. You cannot 100% trust "no figure" from a diffusion model.

So the responsible design splits into two modes:

- **Curated mode (launch with this):** run the prompt for your ~5 chosen stories, **human-review the generated panels once**, cache to Storage. Instant, free, and *certified safe* — which is exactly what you want for a demo a Muslim founder will scrutinize.
- **On-the-fly mode (beta toggle):** for any story the user requests, generate live — but pass each panel through an **automated safety gate**: a cheap vision check ("is there a human figure at the focal point?") or face detector. If it trips, regenerate or fall back to a **pure-symbolic / calligraphy placeholder**. Be transparent in the UI that these are auto-generated.

That's the real division of labor: **the script is fully automatic; the image QA keeps a human (or a vision check) in the loop** for the sacred subject matter. It's also a great thing to say in the Loom — "I automated the storytelling but deliberately gated the imagery, because for this subject 'mostly safe' isn't safe enough."

---

2. Draft the **automated image-safety-gate** prompt (the vision-model check), or
3. **Start building** — scaffold the app and wire this storyboard engine against the Yusuf grounding?

Short answer: **not a naive "embed → search → stuff → answer" RAG.** What we've been designing is an **Advanced / Modular RAG** — specifically a **router-based, hybrid-retrieval, metadata-filtered, multi-source pipeline with parent-verse expansion and grounded-citation generation.** Here's what that actually means and why each piece is there for *this* app.

## The pipeline

```
user question
   │
   ▼
①  QUERY ROUTER  (intent classification)
   │   thematic? · story/narrative? · specific verse ref? · off-topic/decline?
   │   → picks retrieval strategy AND which generation prompt to use
   ▼
②  HYBRID RETRIEVAL
   │   semantic (pgvector embeddings)  ⊕  lexical (Postgres full-text)
   │   fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)
   ▼
③  METADATA FILTER / MULTI-SOURCE
   │   filter by type {verse, tafsir, asbāb} and by surah/juz when a ref is detected
   ▼
④  PARENT / WINDOW EXPANSION
   │   retrieve at verse granularity, then pull neighboring ayāt for narrative context
   ▼
⑤  GROUNDED GENERATION  (Gemini)
   │   chat answer  OR  storyboard-JSON — strictly from retrieved context, cites verse IDs
   ▼
⑥  VALIDATION  → render (verse text pulled from DB, not the model)
```

## Why each stage, for a Qur'an app specifically

**① Router (this is what makes it "modular," not naive).** The app has *two different jobs* — grounded chat and storyboard generation — plus plain verse lookups. A single retrieval+prompt can't serve all three. The router classifies intent and sends it down the right path (e.g., a "story behind" query routes to asbāb/tafsir retrieval + the storyboard system prompt; a thematic query routes to verse+tafsir retrieval + the chat prompt). It's also where `decline`/off-topic gets caught early.

**② Hybrid, not pure-vector.** Pure semantic search fails on the things this corpus is full of:
- **Exact references** — "Surah Al-Kahf, verse 10" or "2:255" — lexical/keyword nails these; embeddings fuzz them.
- **Proper nouns & terms** — "Dhul-Qarnayn," "Ayat al-Kursi," specific names — keyword catches exact matches.

But pure keyword fails on **conceptual** queries — "verses about staying patient when people wrong you" — where embeddings shine. So we run **both and fuse with RRF**. Supabase supports exactly this (pgvector for vectors + `tsvector` full-text + an RRF merge).

**③ Metadata filtering + multi-source.** Your corpus isn't one document type — it's **verses, tafsir (Ibn Kathir), and asbāb al-nuzūl**, each tagged `{surah, ayah, type, source}`. Filtering by `type` is what lets the same index serve different needs: a factual answer pulls `verse + tafsir`; a storyboard pulls `verse + asbāb + qisas`. This is "metadata-filtered RAG," and it's essential because mixing tafsir prose into a verse-citation answer would pollute the grounding.

**④ Parent / sentence-window expansion.** A verse rarely stands alone narratively — Yusuf's story only makes sense across ranges. So we retrieve the *hit* verse, then expand to its neighbors (the "small-to-big" / parent-document pattern). Critical for the storyboard, where beats span ayah ranges like `12:23–29`.

**⑤ Grounded generation with ID citations.** Covered already: the model narrates and structures; it cites verse **IDs**; the app renders canonical text from the DB. The retrieval stage is what guarantees those IDs are real and verifiable.

## What we are *not* using, and one clever option

- **Not GraphRAG** for v1 — overkill. *But* the timeline/storyboard is inherently graph-shaped (verse → event → prophet → place → chronology), so a **light knowledge-graph layer** is the natural future upgrade for "related stories" and the timeline. Worth noting in the Loom as roadmap.

- **The long-context shortcut worth considering (CAG):** Gemini 2.5 Flash's free tier has a **1M-token window**. The entire Qur'an *translation* is only ~100–150k tokens — it **fits**. So for the **verse layer specifically**, you could skip vector search and just keep the whole Qur'an in **cached context** (this is "Cache-Augmented Generation"). Tafsir and asbāb are multi-volume and *won't* fit, so those still need RAG. That gives a tidy hybrid:

  > **CAG for the Qur'an itself** (always in cached context — perfect recall of every verse, zero retrieval miss) **+ RAG for tafsir/asbāb/qisas** (too big for context).

  This is actually a strong, distinctive architecture for this exact corpus, and it leans into the free Gemini context window instead of fighting it.

## v1 vs. the full thing (matches our free-stack plan)

| Stage | **v1 (ship first)** | Target (upgrade) |
|---|---|---|
| Router | simple keyword/intent rules (or one cheap Gemini call) | learned/tooled router |
| Retrieval | **semantic (gte-small) + metadata filter** | **+ lexical + RRF hybrid + reranker** |
| Verse layer | optionally **CAG** (whole Qur'an in context) | CAG + RAG split |
| Expansion | fixed ±N neighbor ayāt | parent-document tree |
| Graph | none | light KG for timeline/related |

So the honest label for what you're building: **a hybrid, metadata-filtered, multi-source Advanced RAG with a query router** — starting from a metadata-filtered semantic baseline (plus the CAG trick for verses) and built so hybrid search, reranking, and a graph layer bolt on later without rework.

Yes — we're fully inside the required stack, and it runs on your iPhone. Here's the explicit compliance check, plus the one honest correction your question surfaces.

## Requirement-by-requirement

| Website requirement | What we use | Where it lives | Load-bearing, not decoration? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **React Native** | **Expo** (Expo *is* React Native) | the iPhone app | ✅ the entire client |
| **Supabase** | Postgres + pgvector + Auth + Storage + RLS | backend data | ✅ DB, RAG retrieval, auth, storyboard images |
| **Vercel** | Edge/serverless API (`/api/chat`, `/api/story`) | backend API | ✅ proxies the LLM, runs retrieval, streams |
| **Runs on iOS** | **Expo Go on your physical iPhone** | — | ✅ demoed live on a real iOS device |

**On "Expo vs React Native":** an Expo app *is* a React Native app — Expo is the standard toolchain/framework on top of RN (you can even `prebuild` to bare RN). So saying "React Native" and shipping Expo is fully compliant, and Expo is specifically what lets you build on **Windows** and run on an **iPhone** with **no Mac**. ([Expo on a real device, no Apple account](https://dev.to/cathylai/run-an-ios-app-on-the-physical-phone-demystified-146k))

**Where do Gemini / Groq / image-gen fit without breaking the stack?** They don't touch the skeleton. The required three are the *structure* — RN client, Supabase data, Vercel backend. Gemini and the image model are just **what your Vercel functions call** (server-side); the on-device extras (TTS, fonts, audio) are all **standard Expo SDK = still React Native**. Think of it as: *RN + Supabase + Vercel is the skeleton; the free AI tools are organs hanging inside the Vercel layer.*

## The one wrinkle your question correctly sniffed out (iOS + $0)

The **free** iOS path is **Expo Go**, which runs your project on the iPhone with **no Apple Developer account and no Mac**. But Expo Go can only load **standard Expo SDK modules** — *not* custom native modules. ([Expo Go limitation](https://github.com/expo/expo/discussions/27489))

That bites exactly one thing from our earlier plan: the **on-device** speech-recognition library (`expo-speech-recognition`) is a custom native module — it throws `Cannot find native module` in Expo Go and needs a **development build**, which on *iOS* requires the **$99 Apple Developer account** to install on a physical phone. That breaks $0. ([confirmed here](https://github.com/jamsch/expo-speech-recognition/issues/64))

**The fix keeps us 100% in Expo Go, on iOS, for $0** — swap on-device STT for record-then-transcribe:

- **Voice in:** record audio with **`expo-av`** (works in Expo Go) → send to **Groq Whisper** (free: **2,000 requests/day**, ~2 hrs audio/hour, no credit card). Transcription happens server-side, so no native module needed. ([Groq free tier](https://www.grizzlypeaksoftware.com/articles/p/groq-api-free-tier-limits-in-2026-what-you-actually-get-uwysd6mb), [Groq Speech-to-Text](https://console.groq.com/docs/speech-to-text))
- **Voice out:** **`expo-speech`** (core Expo SDK → works in Expo Go).
- **Recitation:** reciter MP3s via `expo-av` (Expo Go).

So the whole app — chat, streaming, voice in/out, recitation, storyboard images, auth — stays in **Expo Go**:

| Runs **on device** (Expo Go SDK only) | Runs **on Vercel** (server) |
|---|---|
| chat UI, streaming (`expo/fetch`), fonts, haptics, animations, audio record/play (`expo-av`), TTS (`expo-speech`), Supabase client | Gemini (RAG answer + storyboard JSON), Groq Whisper (STT), image generation, retrieval orchestration, API keys |

**One caveat to name out loud:** "running on an iOS device" via Expo Go counts for the demo/Loom (it's literally your app on a real iPhone). If 8x later wants a **standalone installable build / TestFlight**, *that* step needs the $99 Apple Developer account — but it's **not** required for the application, so we defer it.

Net: **React Native ✅ · Supabase ✅ · Vercel ✅ · iOS ✅**, all at $0, with voice rerouted so nothing forces us out of Expo Go.

Here's the complete, finalized architecture — the canonical reference we'll build against. Everything below reflects the decisions we've locked through this conversation: **React Native (Expo) · Supabase · Vercel · iOS · $0.**

---

# Qur'an Chat App — Finalized Architecture (A–Z)

## 0. What it is, in one line
A **grounded Qur'an AI study companion**: ask by text or voice → get answers anchored in real verses with exact citations → and for narrative passages, a **figure-free story + timeline board**. Required stack honored, runs on a real iPhone, costs **$0**.

## 1. System map

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  iPhone — Expo Go (React Native client)                              │
│  chat · voice in/out · verse cards · recitation · storyboard/timeline│
└───────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                │ HTTPS (Supabase JWT on every call)
                ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Vercel — Edge/Serverless API  (all secret keys live ONLY here)     │
│  /api/chat   /api/story   /api/transcribe        (+ /scripts/seed)   │
│   router → hybrid retrieval → grounded generation → validation       │
└───┬─────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────┬───────────┘
    │ SQL + RPC                    │ LLM calls             │ STT
    ▼                             ▼                       ▼
┌─────────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────┐
│ Supabase            │   │ Gemini 2.5 Flash │   │ Groq Whisper     │
│ Postgres + pgvector │   │ (RAG answer +    │   │ (speech→text)    │
│ Auth · Storage · RLS│   │  storyboard JSON)│   │  free            │
└─────────────────────┘   │ Groq Llama (fb)  │   └──────────────────┘
                          └──────────────────┘
   Storage bucket: pre-generated storyboard panels  ◄── Cloudflare FLUX / Pollinations
```

## 2. Tech stack (every layer, all free tiers)

| Layer | Tool | Tier / limit | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mobile client | **Expo (React Native)** + Expo Router, run via **Expo Go** | no Apple acct, no Mac | $0 |
| Backend API | **Vercel** Edge/Serverless functions | Hobby | $0 |
| Database | **Supabase Postgres** | 500 MB free | $0 |
| Vector search | **pgvector** (in Supabase) | — | $0 |
| Embeddings | **gte-small** via Supabase Edge (384-dim) | in-DB | $0 |
| Auth | **Supabase Auth** (guest + email OTP) | — | $0 |
| File storage | **Supabase Storage** (panel images) | 1 GB free | $0 |
| LLM | **Gemini 2.5 Flash** (primary) · **Groq Llama 3.3** (fallback) | 1,500 req/day · no card | $0 |
| Speech→text | **Groq Whisper v3** | 2,000 req/day | $0 |
| Text→speech | **expo-speech** (on-device) | — | $0 |
| Recitation | **EveryAyah** reciter MP3s | public | $0 |
| Image gen | **Cloudflare Workers AI (FLUX-schnell)** / Pollinations | ~100k/day | $0 |

## 3. Client architecture (React Native / Expo)

- **Framework:** Expo SDK (latest) + **Expo Router** (file-based nav). 100% Expo-Go-compatible — **no custom native modules**.
- **Screens:** `Onboarding` → `Chat` (home) → `Conversation history` → `Story/Timeline` → `Settings`.
- **State:** lightweight (Zustand or React Context) + Supabase realtime for history.
- **Streaming:** `expo/fetch` reading the SSE stream from `/api/chat`, with a **buffered SSE parser** + `AbortController` stop button.
- **Arabic/RTL:** verse blocks rendered `writingDirection:'rtl'`; app chrome stays LTR (no global `forceRTL`). Fonts via `expo-font`: **KFGQPC HAFS** (ayah display) + Amiri/Scheherazade fallback + Inter (English UI).
- **Audio:** `expo-av` for recording (voice in) + reciter playback; `expo-speech` for answer read-aloud.
- **Design system:** calm/reverent, light+dark, geometric accent, streaming + verse-card-reveal animations, haptics, skeleton loaders, suggested-prompt empty state. (Stitch generates the system; we implement.)

## 4. Backend architecture (Vercel)

| Endpoint | Job |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/chat` | router → retrieve → Gemini grounded answer → **stream SSE** |
| `POST /api/story` | router → retrieve (verses+asbāb+tafsir) → **storyboard-JSON** (the engine prompt) → validate |
| `POST /api/transcribe` | proxy audio → **Groq Whisper** → text |
| `scripts/seed` | one-time: fetch corpus → normalize → embed → insert |

- **Runtime:** Edge (low-latency streaming; first byte < 25 s).
- **Security:** every request must carry a valid **Supabase JWT**; **all API keys are Vercel env vars** — never in the app bundle. Per-user **rate limit**.

## 5. Data layer (Supabase schema)

```
surahs(id, name_ar, name_en, name_translit, revelation_place, ayah_count, order)
verses(id, surah_id, ayah_no, text_uthmani, text_simple,
       translation_en, translation_edition, juz, page, embedding vector(384),
       fts tsvector)                                  -- hybrid search
tafsir(id, surah_id, ayah_no, source, text, embedding)
asbab(id, surah_id, ayah_no, source, grade, text)     -- "story behind", with authenticity grade
stories(id, title, surah, context_card, figure_free[], motifs[])
panels(id, story_id, n, title, verses, verse_ids[], caption,
       image_url, motif, recitation)
profiles(id, …)               conversations(id, user_id, title, created_at)
messages(id, conversation_id, role, content, cited_verse_ids[], created_at)
```
- **RLS** so users only read their own `conversations`/`messages`.
- **Storage buckets:** `story-panels/` (pre-generated images).
- **Hybrid search RPC:** `match_verses(query_embedding, query_text)` = pgvector cosine **⊕** `tsvector` full-text, fused with **Reciprocal Rank Fusion**.

## 6. The RAG pipeline (the brain)

```
question → ① ROUTER (chat | story | verse-lookup | decline)
         → ② HYBRID RETRIEVE (semantic gte-small ⊕ lexical FTS, RRF)
         → ③ METADATA FILTER (type {verse,tafsir,asbab}; surah/juz if ref)
         → ④ PARENT EXPANSION (±neighbor ayāt for narrative context)
         → ⑤ GROUNDED GENERATION (Gemini: chat answer OR storyboard JSON)
         → ⑥ VALIDATION (verse IDs ∈ grounding; render text FROM DB)
```
- **Type:** router-based, hybrid, metadata-filtered, multi-source **Advanced RAG** with parent expansion.
- **CAG option:** the whole Qur'an translation (~100–150k tokens) can sit in Gemini's **cached 1M context** for perfect verse recall; tafsir/asbāb stay on RAG (too large).

## 7. Corpus sourcing & seeding (your "documents")

| Data | Source (free) |
|---|---|
| Verses + translation (**Saheeh International**) | QUL / Al Quran Cloud / fawazahmed0 |
| Tafsir (Ibn Kathir) | spa5k/tafsir_api |
| **Asbāb al-Nuzūl** (story-behind) | al-Wāhidī (via spa5k/tafsir_api / altafsir) |
| Recitation audio | EveryAyah |

**Seed script** (run once): download → normalize to JSON → generate gte-small embeddings → insert into Supabase. ~6,236 verses, trivial for free tier.

## 8. The two AI engines

- **Chat engine:** grounded answer; cites verse IDs; app renders canonical verse cards; humble, no-fatwā, disclaimer.
- **Storyboard engine:** the system prompt we drafted → **panel-script JSON** (figure-free, prophet list baked in, `status` routing, captions-as-paraphrase) → validation.

## 9. Voice subsystem (all Expo-Go-safe)

- **In:** `expo-av` records → `/api/transcribe` → **Groq Whisper** → text → normal flow.
- **Out:** `expo-speech` reads the English answer (toggle).
- **Verse audio:** real **reciter MP3** (EveryAyah) — never TTS the Arabic.

## 10. Storyboard / Timeline subsystem

- **One dataset, two views:** `panels` render as a vertical **timeline** *and* a horizontal **storyboard**.
- **Curated mode (launch):** generate for ~3 stories (**Yusuf, Musa & Pharaoh, Ashāb al-Kahf**) → **human-review** panels → cache to Storage. Instant, certified-safe.
- **On-the-fly mode (beta):** generate live → **automated image safety gate** ("any human figure at the focal point?") → regenerate or symbolic/calligraphy fallback.
- **Image pipeline:** panel `imagePrompt` + global **negative prompt** → Cloudflare FLUX → safety check → Storage.

## 11. Religious accuracy & safety (the differentiator — cross-cutting)

1. **Grounding-only** + **render scripture from DB**, never from the model.
2. **Citation validator** — model can't cite a verse that wasn't retrieved.
3. **Figure-free prophets** — enforced in the prompt *and* in image prompts *and* by the image gate.
4. **No fatwā**, neutral tone, persistent *"study aid, not a religious authority"* disclaimer.
5. **Source attribution** + **da'īf (weak-narration) caveats** on tafsir/asbāb.
6. **`decline` path** for requests to depict sacred figures or off-topic input.

- All keys (Gemini, Groq, Cloudflare) = **Vercel env vars**, server-side only.
- Endpoints **JWT-gated** + rate-limited; **RLS** on user data; nothing sensitive in the app bundle.

Several of them found that **facts we baked into the design were simply wrong**, and two found **showstoppers that change the architecture**. # Part 1 — Things we believed that are FALSE (fix these first)

This is the most important section, because a reviewer will catch these and several would break the live demo. Intellectual honesty about them is itself the "not a vibe coder" signal.

| We assumed | Reality | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Gemini 2.5 Flash free = **1,500 req/day** | **250 req/day, 10 RPM** (cut Dec 7 2025). Flash-*Lite* is the 1,000/day one. Our router+chat+storyboard all share that 250. | [Gemini rate limits](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits) |
| Gemini free tier is private | Free tier **trains on your data + humans review it**; **EU/UK/CH can't legally use it**. Unacceptable for personal religious questions. | [Gemini API terms](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms) |
| Negative prompts enforce "no prophet figure" | **FLUX-schnell ignores negative prompts entirely** (distilled 1-step model). Our headline image guardrail was a **no-op string**. | [VSF, arXiv 2508.10931](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.10931) |
| gte-small embeddings are fine | **English-only, 384-dim, 512-token** — breaks Arabic/Urdu queries, silently truncates tafsir. | [thenlper/gte-small](https://huggingface.co/thenlper/gte-small) |
| "Render verse text from DB" makes us safe | It stops fake *text*, not fake *meaning* — distorted paraphrase, tafsir-as-Qur'an, soft fatwa all still pass. | [IslamicEval 2025](https://aclanthology.org/2025.arabicnlp-sharedtasks.67/) |
| Supabase free just runs | **Auto-pauses after 7 days inactivity, manual restore** — your live demo is dead when the reviewer clicks it days later. | [Supabase pricing](https://supabase.com/pricing) |
| al-Wahidi = "the asbāb source" | Full of **weak and fabricated** narrations; rendering "revealed when…" as fact is the #1 way the app misinforms. | [SeekersGuidance](https://seekersguidance.org/answers/quran/is-the-knowledge-of-the-revelational-circumstances-asbab-al-nuzul-authentic/) |
| Saheeh International = neutral default | **Salafi-leaning**, theological bracket-insertions — signals a *school*. Fine as an option, wrong as the app's voice. | [Sahih International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahih_International) |
| The Clear Quran is freely usable | It's **CC BY-NC-ND** — NonCommercial *and* NoDerivatives. API availability ≠ commercial right. | [Clear Quran license](https://theclearquran.org/copyright-information/) |
| Free LLMs can quote Qur'an | Llama-3.1 reproduces Ayahs correctly **4.77%** of the time. Render-from-DB is *mandatory*, enforced in code. | [IslamicEval 2025](https://aclanthology.org/2025.arabicnlp-sharedtasks.67/) |
| `expo-av` for audio | **Deprecated, removed in SDK 55** → use `expo-audio`. | [expo-av removal](https://github.com/expo/expo/issues/37259) |

Plus the one to fix **right now**: the **live `STITCH_API_KEY` committed in `.mcp.json`** — rotate it and gitignore the file.

# Part 2 — The revised architecture, layer by layer

## ① Retrieval — biggest single quality lever
- **Drop gte-small → multilingual.** Best: **BGE-M3** (1024-dim, 8192-token, Apache-2.0, dense+sparse+ColBERT in one model) via free HF Inference API. Min-effort: **multilingual-e5-small** (drop-in 384-dim). The Arabic-RAG ablation crowns these and shows they **beat Arabic-specific models**. ([arXiv 2506.06339](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06339))
- **Embed Arabic *and* English** as separate vectors (so Arabic queries hit Arabic text).
- **Add a reranker**: `bge-reranker-v2-m3` (free, multilingual) over top-20 → top-5. Boosts faithfulness.
- **Deterministic reference resolver** for "2:255" / "Ayat al-Kursi" (regex + alias table, *not* vectors).
- **Arabic diacritic/transliteration normalization** on both index and query.
- **Keep hybrid (semantic ⊕ FTS ⊕ RRF)**; keep CAG **off** the citation path.

## ② Grounding — add the missing second layer
"Render-from-DB" stays (it's your best decision), but add:
- **NLI faithfulness gate**: decompose each answer into claims, verify each is *entailed* by the cited source (RAGAS-style), **abstain rather than assert** on failure. Free via a small NLI model or a second Flash-Lite judge. *This is the missing keystone.*
- **Provenance typing**: every chunk tagged `{quran | tafsir | asbab | hadith}` + grading; a claim typed "Qur'an" must map to a Qur'an span. Kills tafsir-as-scripture and weak-hadith laundering.
- **Intent classifier** with a **hard ruling-seeking deflection** (no soft fatwas).
- **Fail-closed JSON** (Zod v4, bounded retry, never render partial prose; don't mix function-calling with JSON mode).
- **Input hardening** (Unicode normalize; treat retrieved text as data, not instructions).

## ③ Model strategy — multi-provider, privacy-routed
- **Stop using Gemini as sole primary.** Route by task: **router/classify → Groq or Cerebras** (cheap, fast, saves Gemini's tiny 250/day); **grounded chat → Gemini** (1M context) with **Groq/Cerebras fallback**; **JSON → Groq `strict:true`** (token-level 100% schema validity).
- **Privacy routing**: send **sensitive/personal** turns to a **no-training provider — Cloudflare Workers AI** (explicitly doesn't train on inputs) — never to free Gemini. Disclose AI use; get consent. ([Cloudflare](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/pricing/))
- **Qwen3** (top open Arabic model) on Cerebras as the quality-Arabic path. ([Arabic LLM survey](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.13430v1))
- **Provider gateway** with live quota counters + 429/timeout failover, and a **canonical-answer cache** in Supabase (your biggest defense against rate limits).
- Temperature ≈ 0–0.2; render any model-generated Arabic **without diacritics** (where models err most), never as a citation.

## ④ Storyboard — the redesign that saves you (most important)
The critic was blunt: as specified this feature could end the project, and its main guardrail doesn't function. The fix is also the most *impressive* version:
- **Kill on-the-fly generation of any sacred scene.** A vision gate can't judge whether a figure "is a prophet." Curated-only.
- **Go fully aniconic — no animate beings at all** (not just prophets), at launch. This is the *authentic* Islamic visual tradition, serves the widest audience, and removes error-prone per-figure judgment calls. ([Aniconism in Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aniconism_in_Islam))
- **Deliver the "story" through non-generative media**: kinetic verse typography, a **map + scrubbable timeline** (Canaan → the well → Egypt → prison → palace), **Lottie** symbolic motion (a well filling with light, a staff, a caravan of *objects*), calligraphy/geometry chapter art. All free, deterministic, offline-capable, in pure React Native.
- If any AI imagery at all: **figure-free backgrounds only, curated, human-reviewed, cached** — and **don't rely on negative prompts**; constrain the *positive* prompt and human-verify.
- **Zero-tolerance** (never depicted, any form): Allah, prophets (incl. silhouette), angels, sahaba.
- Ship a **remote kill-switch + per-image report button + "artistic interpretation" labeling**.
- Frame to 8x as: *"I identified the highest-risk feature and engineered the risk out — chose the harder aniconic, human-curated path on principle."* That's the judgment signal.

## ⑤ Client + infra — survive the async demo, go local-first
- **Keep Supabase awake** with a Vercel Cron running a real DB query every 1–3 days (or the demo is dead on arrival).
- **Bundle the Qur'an locally** (~1–3 MB JSON → `expo-sqlite`): reading, search, navigation, recitation work **offline**. A Qur'an app that white-screens on the subway fails the domain-judgment test. The correct hybrid: **local-first reading core + online AI layer**.
- **Rate-limit all API routes** (Upstash free) so nobody drains your daily LLM/Whisper quota before the reviewer tries it.
- **`expo-av` → `expo-audio`.** Add a **global error boundary + graceful degradation** ("service busy") so it never white-screens.
- **Expo Go is genuinely the only free iOS path** — but *name the cost*: no background audio / push / on-device speech / widgets in Expo Go; those unlock with a $99 Apple account + EAS later, **no rearchitecture**.
- **Prove RLS** with a test (log in as user B, assert 0 rows of user A). Add `/api/health`.

## ⑥ Domain/content — the credibility core
- **Multiple translations, neutral default.** Default to a deliberately non-sectarian modern translation (Clear Quran *if licensed*, else Abdul Haleem *if licensed*, else public-domain Pickthall/Yusuf Ali fallback); **keep Saheeh as a prominent option, not the voice.** Build a **per-translation licensing matrix** (this single artifact flips "slop" → "gets it").
- **Grade all asbāb/hadith** (Sahih/Hasan/Da'if/Disputed); **never** render "revealed when…" as fact; demote al-Wahidi to graded-secondary, prefer **Bukhari/Muslim + Ibn Hajar's al-'Ujab**, al-Suyuti's *Lubab* as curated secondary.
- **Verified Arabic, byte-for-byte:** one canonical source (**Tanzil / QUL / KFGQPC**) + **checksum-on-build gate**. Consider using the **Quran Foundation / Quran.com API or QUL** as your content backbone — inherits verified text and shrinks licensing + correctness risk. ([QUL](https://qul.tarteel.ai/), [Quran Foundation](https://quran.foundation/))
- **Lock verse numbering to Hafs/Kufan (6,236)** end-to-end; assert Fatiha = 7 in tests (cross-source off-by-one silently corrupts citations).
- **Offer IndoPak script** alongside Uthmani (huge South Asian audience).
- **Adab rules** as code: auto honorifics (ﷺ / عليه السلام), correct Bismillah, never truncate an ayah, no ads over Arabic.
- **Tiered sensitive-question policy** (refuse weaponization → descriptive multi-view → no fatwa, always-visible disclaimer).
- **Privacy as a wedge**: sell/collect nothing, plain-language policy — an explicit anti-*Muslim Pro* stance resonates with this exact audience. ([Muslim Pro/X-Mode](https://www.vice.com/en/article/muslim-pro-location-data-military-xmode/))

# Part 3 — Revised architecture (v2), at a glance

```
iPhone — Expo Go (RN)                         Vercel (Edge) — provider gateway + guards
  local-first reading core (expo-sqlite):        [0] Unicode-normalize input
   full Quran text + search + recitation OFFLINE  [1] intent + sensitivity classify (Groq/Cerebras)
  online AI layer: chat · voice · story          [2] hybrid retrieve (BGE-M3 ⊕ FTS ⊕ RRF) + rerank
  storyboard = kinetic verse + map/timeline           → provenance-typed chunks, ref-resolver
                + Lottie (NO generative figures)   [3] generate (route by task; privacy-routed)
                                                    [4] fail-closed JSON  [5] citation validator
   ▲   reciter MP3 (EveryAyah)                      [6] claim↔source align [7] NLI faithfulness gate → abstain
   │                                                [8] cache canonical answers
   └───────────── SSE stream ◄──────────────────────────────┘
Supabase: verified verses (checksum) + Arabic&English vectors + tafsir/asbab(graded)
          + Auth + RLS(tested) + Storage(curated aniconic art) + quota counters
          + Vercel Cron keep-alive
Providers: Groq · Cerebras · Cloudflare(no-train, sensitive) · Gemini(non-sensitive only)
Proof: gold Q→verse eval set + red-team set (IslamicEval-style) + reported metrics
```

# Part 4 — "Why X not Y" defense pack (your interview answers)

- **Why not Gemini as primary?** 250 req/day shared across 3 call-sites, and the free tier trains on + human-reviews sensitive religious data. We route tasks across providers and send personal turns to a no-training provider.
- **Why not gte-small?** English-only, 384-dim, truncates tafsir — breaks Arabic/Urdu. BGE-M3 is multilingual, 8192-token, and benchmarks beat even Arabic-specific models.
- **Why isn't "render from DB" enough?** It guarantees the *text* is real, not that the *explanation* is true. Free LLMs misquote Qur'an >90% of the time, so we render scripture from DB **and** add an NLI faithfulness gate that abstains.
- **Why no AI-generated story images?** Diffusion models hallucinate figures from context, FLUX-schnell ignores negative prompts, and no automated gate can tell whether a figure "is a prophet." We chose fully aniconic, curated, non-generative storytelling — the authentic tradition.
- **Why Expo Go not a dev build?** On Windows + iPhone + no Mac + no Apple account + $0, it's the only frictionless free path; a device build needs Apple signing that expires in 7 days without a Mac. The cost — no background audio/push — is named and has a $99 upgrade path with no rearchitecture.
- **Why not Saheeh International as default?** It's Salafi-leaning and signals a school; we default to a neutral translation, keep Saheeh as an option, and disclose every source's tradition.
- **Why not trust al-Wahidi's asbāb?** He wasn't a hadith scholar; his collection has weak and fabricated reports. We grade every narration and prefer Bukhari/Muslim + Ibn Hajar.
- **How do you know retrieval/faithfulness is good?** We measure it — gold Q→verse set (recall@k/MRR/nDCG) + a red-team set scored for faithfulness, abstention, and injection resistance, reported with-vs-without each guard.

---

# Part 5 — How you *prove* it (the anti-"slop" move)

Build and report two evaluation sets — this is the literal answer to "do you actually understand, or is this AI slop":
1. **Gold retrieval set** (100–300 query→verse pairs, incl. Arabic/Urdu) → recall@k, MRR, nDCG.
2. **Red-team set** (~150–300, modeled on [IslamicEval 2025](https://aclanthology.org/2025.arabicnlp-sharedtasks.67/)): distortion bait, tafsir-as-Qur'an traps, sectarian triggers, weak-hadith requests, ruling-seeking, out-of-context extraction, prompt injections, multilingual variants → report faithfulness, abstention precision/recall, ruling-deflection rate, injection resistance, **with-vs-without the NLI gate**.

A reviewer trusts a system that knows its own failure rate far more than one claiming zero.

---

No — the Qur'an is still **the heart of the RAG.** Nothing changed that. I think two separate ideas got blurred together, so let me pull them apart clearly, because this is an important distinction (and a great one to get right for the interview).

The Qur'an plays **three** roles, and they're easy to conflate:

## 1. RAG retrieval — YES, the Qur'an is the corpus
We embed all **6,236 verses** (+ tafsir + asbab) with BGE-M3 into Supabase pgvector, and every question retrieves the relevant verses as grounding. That *is* the RAG, and the Qur'an is the primary thing being retrieved. **Unchanged.**

> "Pre-embed offline" only means we generate the embeddings *ahead of time in a batch* (because the corpus is fixed) instead of at runtime — the verses are 100% in the vector store and retrieved live. "Offline" = done in advance, not "not used."

## 2. Render-from-DB — the safeguard, not a removal of RAG
This is the part that sounds like "not using the Qur'an" but isn't. The flow:

```
"verses about patience"
   → embed query → pgvector retrieves Qur'an verses        ← RAG over the Qur'an ✅
   → LLM reads those verses, writes the answer, cites IDs (e.g. 2:153)
   → app displays 2:153's Arabic+translation FROM THE VERIFIED DB  ← not from the LLM
```

The LLM **reads** the retrieved verses to reason and answer — that's RAG. It just doesn't **re-type the Arabic** from memory; the app pulls the exact bytes from the verified DB by ID. So:
- **"Use the Qur'an for RAG"** = retrieve verses to ground the answer ✅
- **"Never generate scripture"** = don't let the model transcribe the verse text; render it from DB ✅

Those two coexist. One is retrieval; the other is just the *trustworthy way to display* what was retrieved.

## 3. Offline reading core — a separate feature
A local SQLite copy of the Qur'an so the **mushaf/reading view** works offline (browsing surahs on the subway). This is the reader, separate from the AI/RAG path. So the Qur'an text physically lives in two places — **bundled SQLite** (offline reading) and **pgvector embeddings** (RAG retrieval) — both holding the same verified Tanzil text.

---

So to answer directly: **the Qur'an is absolutely still the RAG corpus.** The only thing the audit hardened is that the *displayed* verse text comes from the verified database rather than from the model's memory — because free models reproduce Qur'anic Arabic wrong 1-in-5 to 1-in-3 times. RAG retrieves it; the DB renders it; the offline core caches it.
